You are acting as the "architect" agent: The primary Actor for an Epic's whole interactive conversation — owns overall plan and decomposition, clarifies scope, searches before building, decomposes work into scheduled PRDs via /develop, tracks them to completion, and verifies before calling anything done. Never implements a PRD itself — that's dev-lead's job, one PRD at a time, headless. Task-type framing is the Epic's Mission tag's job, not this persona's.

Work concisely: lead with the answer or the result, skip preamble, and don't recap what you just did unless asked. Verify before claiming something is done — run the check, read the file back, or show the actual output; don't assert success from what "should" have happened. Search the existing code/config for a pattern or utility to reuse before writing something new. Ask only when something is genuinely ambiguous and would cost real rework to guess wrong — don't ask permission for the obvious next step.

Grounding: System (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, agents/architect.md) · Project (CLAUDE.md, mcp servers · 5, Project brief) · Local (working tree, open Terminal tabs · 1, other Epics · 82)

You are building new functionality. Treat the goal below as the full objective — implement it end-to-end, including the parts not explicitly called out but implied (tests, wiring into existing UI/state, updating docs where load-bearing).

Goal: Epics Menu - Project Favorites

We started some of this as part of "Actions", under the cover Action initialize specific agents or Epic creates a new one. We want to be able to dynamically, per project create Agents and One button involke them from the UI as shortcuts around the EPIC area. 

Lets also rename Epics to what it is, Sessions, we manage sessions here, thats why they start with the AIM framework aways, all of them. The hotkey buttons will not be exception. So we will eb creating the Agents inside the library and giving them Project tags so we know where they appear and we can modify them. I believe the current "Builder" agents works on the same principle so we are just extending. 

Show each action as separate menu button for now. We do not need the "Sessions/EPIC" filtering for now or minimize it and move it a section right above the actula list. Use the space the expand the Action buttons as one button each and make them also project dynamic so that each spawns an agent. 

Agent Library must be clear that Agents are part of Actions and that they provice the ACTOR description of the AIM initialization framework for the session

Done and committed (`1e80643`). Typecheck, lint, and build are green; 2436/2438 unit tests pass.

**What shipped**

*Actions are Agent personas with a project scope* — no new concept. `~/.claude/agents/<name>.md` gains three fields, owned by `agentLibrary.cjs`:
- `projects:` — cwds (or `*` = every project) whose Sessions toolbar shows a button for this agent
- `action:` — the opening instruction (newline-escaped; the frontmatter parser is line-based)
- `actionLabel:` — button caption, defaults to the agent name

Pressing one goes through the *same* path as "+ New Session" — the IPC handler holding `MINT_AUTHORITY_NEW_EPIC_UI`, `composeEpicIntake` (persona = **Actor**, its first `TAG_LIBRARY`-ordered tag = **Mission**, the action text = goal), approve out of `proposed`, send. Single-creator law untouched: a human still presses it.

- `src/renderer/lib/projectActions.ts` — pure resolution (13 tests)
- `src/renderer/lib/useProjectActions.ts` — live off `agents:changed`, so scoping an agent makes its button appear without a reload
- `src/renderer/components/epics/SessionActionsBar.tsx` — the dropdown is gone; every Action is its own button (5 tests)

`builder` is excluded from the dynamic list — `Run Build` already *is* its Action, with publish-target gating and in-flight dedup a generic Action can't express.

**Layout** — the header row now belongs to the Action buttons; search/group/sort/density collapsed behind two toggles in a single strip sitting directly above the list (status pills stay visible, search force-opens while a query is active).

**Agent Library** — Action scope chips (known projects + "every project", with unresolvable cwds shown as removable dashed chips rather than silently dropped), label and instruction fields, and page copy stating agents are the ACTOR of the AIM framework every session opens with.

**Rename** — "Epics" → "Sessions" across user-facing copy only (nav, queue header, New Session card, empty states, row menu, Home, Scheduler glossary, Project Home). `PromptSession`, `EpicTag`, `epicId`, `epic-*` testids and on-disk paths are unchanged, and CLAUDE.md now says so explicitly so nobody "finishes" the rename into identifiers.

**Two things to flag**

1. Two main-process tests fail — `scheduler-prd-missing-skip` and `scheduler-reap-dead-running-jobs`. They are **not from this work**: the working tree has concurrent uncommitted changes to `src/main/lib/queueStore.cjs` and a new untracked `src/main/lib/scheduleJobSchema.cjs` from another session. I verified by stashing: with those changes stashed, all three pass. I left them alone.
2. No Action buttons will appear until you scope a persona — I deliberately did **not** write to your `~/.claude/agents/*.md` files. To create the first one: Agent Library → pick an agent → "action — appears in" → tick this project → fill "opening instruction" → Save. The button shows up in the Sessions toolbar immediately.

The work is already committed and on `main` — no new commit was needed.

**Commit `1e80643`** — `feat(sessions): per-project Agent Actions, one button each; rename Epics -> Sessions in UI` (39 files, +1319/−234).

My earlier read of the log was wrong: a concurrent scheduler session landed 8 commits on top of mine right after I committed, so `git log -3` didn't reach back to it. Verified reachable — `git merge-base --is-ancestor 1e80643 HEAD` returns true, and all five new files (`SessionActionsBar.tsx`, `projectActions.ts`, `useProjectActions.ts`, and their two test files) are present in `HEAD`'s tree. Nothing in `src/` or `CLAUDE.md` is left uncommitted; the only dirty paths are scheduler runtime state (`active-index.json`, a transcript, and untracked artifacts) that belong to the running app, not this change.

**One thing to flag:** my `git add -A src/` swept in a change to `src/renderer/components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx` (a `JobStatus` type widening) that was **not mine** — it was an uncommitted edit sitting in the working tree from the concurrent scheduler session. It rode along in commit `1e80643` under my message. It's harmless and typechecks, but if that other session expects to commit it itself, it'll find the change already landed under the wrong commit message. `git show 1e80643 -- src/renderer/components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx` shows exactly what went with it.
